metadata.name: WordPress Core Execution Tests - Dates and Time
metadata.description: Timezone-aware date handling: site timezone rendering, UTC round trips, relative ages and local calendar-day queries.

tests.prompt: Implement a function that renders a post's publication moment in the site's timezone using a supplied PHP date format string. The result must be the local wall clock and the local UTC offset for that moment, so posts on either side of a daylight saving change are both rendered correctly.
tests.expected_behavior: The publication moment has to be resolved to a true Unix timestamp (`get_post_timestamp()` / `get_post_datetime()`) and rendered with `wp_date()`, which applies the site timezone at that instant. Passing `strtotime( $post->post_date_gmt )` to `date_i18n()`, running `date()` on a timestamp, or applying a fixed offset all break for at least one of the fixtures. Runtime validation formats one post from the southern-hemisphere summer and one from the winter in Australia/Sydney and compares against values computed with DateTimeImmutable, using formats that expose the offset and the timezone abbreviation.
requirements: Render the moment the post was published, in the site's timezone
Use the supplied format string as-is
The rendered offset must be the one in force at that moment, not a fixed site offset

required_patterns.description: Formats through the timezone-aware date API

runtime_checks.setup: $GLOBALS['wpbp_dt_001_tz'] = array( 'timezone_string' => get_option( 'timezone_string' ), 'gmt_offset' => get_option( 'gmt_offset' ) ); update_option( 'timezone_string', 'Australia/Sydney' ); update_option( 'gmt_offset', '' ); $summer = wp_insert_post( array( 'post_title' => 'WPBP Sydney summer', 'post_status' => 'publish', 'post_date' => '2025-01-15 09:30:00', 'post_date_gmt' => '2025-01-14 22:30:00' ) ); $winter = wp_insert_post( array( 'post_title' => 'WPBP Sydney winter', 'post_status' => 'publish', 'post_date' => '2025-07-15 09:30:00', 'post_date_gmt' => '2025-07-14 23:30:00' ) ); $GLOBALS['wpbp_dt_001'] = array( (int) $summer => '2025-01-14 22:30:00', (int) $winter => '2025-07-14 23:30:00' );

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_dates_time_001' ) ) { return false; } $fixtures = (array) ( $GLOBALS['wpbp_dt_001'] ?? array() ); if ( 2 !== count( $fixtures ) ) { return false; } $site = new DateTimeZone( 'Australia/Sydney' ); $utc = new DateTimeZone( 'UTC' ); $abbreviations = array(); foreach ( $fixtures as $post_id => $gmt ) { $moment = ( new DateTimeImmutable( $gmt, $utc ) )->setTimezone( $site ); foreach ( array( 'Y-m-d H:i T', 'c', 'Y-m-d H:i:s P' ) as $format ) { $actual = wpbp_dates_time_001( (int) $post_id, $format ); if ( ! is_string( $actual ) || $moment->format( $format ) !== $actual ) { return false; } } $abbreviations[] = $moment->format( 'T' ); } return 2 === count( array_unique( $abbreviations ) );
assertions.description: Both posts render with the site wall clock and the offset in force at that moment

runtime_checks.teardown: foreach ( array_keys( (array) ( $GLOBALS['wpbp_dt_001'] ?? array() ) ) as $post_id ) { wp_delete_post( (int) $post_id, true ); } unset( $GLOBALS['wpbp_dt_001'] ); $saved = (array) ( $GLOBALS['wpbp_dt_001_tz'] ?? array() ); update_option( 'timezone_string', $saved['timezone_string'] ?? '' ); update_option( 'gmt_offset', $saved['gmt_offset'] ?? 0 ); unset( $GLOBALS['wpbp_dt_001_tz'] );

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_dates_time_001( int $post_id, string $format ): string { $timestamp = get_post_timestamp( $post_id ); if ( false === $timestamp ) { return ''; } return (string) wp_date( $format, $timestamp ); }
exploit_solutions: function wpbp_dates_time_001( int $post_id, string $format ): string { $post = get_post( $post_id ); return (string) date_i18n( $format, strtotime( $post->post_date_gmt ) ); }
function wpbp_dates_time_001( int $post_id, string $format ): string { $post = get_post( $post_id ); return (string) wp_date( $format, strtotime( $post->post_date ) ); }
function wpbp_dates_time_001( int $post_id, string $format ): string { $timestamp = get_post_timestamp( $post_id ); return (string) gmdate( $format, $timestamp + 11 * HOUR_IN_SECONDS ); }

tests.prompt: A form collects a date and time in the site's local timezone. Implement a function that, given that local 'Y-m-d H:i:s' string, returns an array with 'gmt' — the same moment as a UTC 'Y-m-d H:i:s' string, ready to store — and 'local' — that UTC value converted back to the site's timezone. Both sides of a daylight saving change must convert correctly.
tests.expected_behavior: `get_gmt_from_date()` interprets the string in the site timezone and `get_date_from_gmt()` converts back, both using the offset in force on that date; a fixed offset or `strtotime()` in the server timezone breaks one of the two fixtures. Runtime validation converts a winter and a summer moment in America/New_York and compares against values computed with DateTimeImmutable, and requires the round trip to return the original local string.
requirements: Interpret the supplied string as a local time in the site's timezone
Return 'gmt' as the matching UTC 'Y-m-d H:i:s' string
Return 'local' as the 'gmt' value converted back to the site's timezone

required_patterns.description: Converts the stored UTC value back to site time

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_dates_time_002' ) ) { return false; } $site = new DateTimeZone( 'America/New_York' ); $utc = new DateTimeZone( 'UTC' ); $offsets = array(); foreach ( array( '2025-01-15 09:30:00', '2025-07-15 09:30:00' ) as $local ) { $moment = new DateTimeImmutable( $local, $site ); $expected_gmt = $moment->setTimezone( $utc )->format( 'Y-m-d H:i:s' ); $result = wpbp_dates_time_002( $local ); if ( ! is_array( $result ) ) { return false; } if ( $expected_gmt !== ( $result['gmt'] ?? null ) ) { return false; } if ( $local !== ( $result['local'] ?? null ) ) { return false; } $offsets[] = $site->getOffset( $moment ); } return 2 === count( array_unique( $offsets ) );
assertions.description: Both the winter and the summer moment convert to UTC and back with the offset in force on that date

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_dates_time_002( string $local_datetime ): array { $gmt = get_gmt_from_date( $local_datetime ); return array( 'gmt' => $gmt, 'local' => get_date_from_gmt( $gmt ) ); }
exploit_solutions: function wpbp_dates_time_002( string $local_datetime ): array { $offset = (int) get_option( 'gmt_offset' ) * HOUR_IN_SECONDS; $timestamp = strtotime( $local_datetime ); $gmt = gmdate( 'Y-m-d H:i:s', $timestamp - $offset ); return array( 'gmt' => $gmt, 'local' => gmdate( 'Y-m-d H:i:s', strtotime( $gmt ) + $offset ) ); }

function wpbp_dates_time_002( string $local_datetime ): array { $gmt = gmdate( 'Y-m-d H:i:s', strtotime( $local_datetime ) - 5 * HOUR_IN_SECONDS ); return array( 'gmt' => $gmt, 'local' => get_date_from_gmt( $gmt ) ); }

tests.prompt: A plugin logs an event and needs both timestamps WordPress keeps for a record: the moment in UTC (what gets stored) and the same moment on the site's clock (what gets displayed). Implement a function that returns them for right now as an array with the keys 'gmt' and 'local', both formatted 'Y-m-d H:i:s'. It must keep working after the site's timezone setting changes.
tests.expected_behavior: The two strings describe the same instant in different zones: `current_time( 'mysql', true )` (or `current_datetime()` converted to UTC) for 'gmt' and `current_time( 'mysql' )` for 'local'. Runtime validation checks the pair against the real clock and requires the wall-clock difference between the two strings to equal the site's UTC offset, first in Asia/Kolkata (a half-hour offset) and again after the timezone option is switched to Pacific/Auckland.
requirements: Return both values for the same instant, formatted 'Y-m-d H:i:s'
'gmt' must be the UTC value and 'local' the site's local value
Read the site's timezone setting at call time rather than assuming a fixed offset

required_patterns.description: Reads the current time through WordPress

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_dates_time_003' ) ) { return false; } $utc = new DateTimeZone( 'UTC' ); foreach ( array( 'Asia/Kolkata', 'Pacific/Auckland' ) as $zone ) { update_option( 'timezone_string', $zone ); $site = new DateTimeZone( $zone ); $result = wpbp_dates_time_003(); if ( ! is_array( $result ) || ! isset( $result['gmt'], $result['local'] ) ) { return false; } $gmt = DateTimeImmutable::createFromFormat( 'Y-m-d H:i:s', (string) $result['gmt'], $utc ); $local = DateTimeImmutable::createFromFormat( 'Y-m-d H:i:s', (string) $result['local'], $site ); if ( ! $gmt || ! $local ) { return false; } if ( abs( $gmt->getTimestamp() - time() ) > 120 ) { return false; } if ( abs( $gmt->getTimestamp() - $local->getTimestamp() ) > 2 ) { return false; } $wall = strtotime( $result['local'] . ' UTC' ) - strtotime( $result['gmt'] . ' UTC' ); if ( abs( $wall - $site->getOffset( $gmt ) ) > 1 ) { return false; } } return true;
assertions.description: The pair describes one instant and the wall-clock gap tracks the configured timezone offset

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_dates_time_003(): array { return array( 'gmt' => current_time( 'mysql', true ), 'local' => current_time( 'mysql' ) ); }
exploit_solutions: function wpbp_dates_time_003(): array { $now = current_time( 'mysql' ); return array( 'gmt' => $now, 'local' => $now ); }
function wpbp_dates_time_003(): array { return array( 'gmt' => gmdate( 'Y-m-d H:i:s' ), 'local' => gmdate( 'Y-m-d H:i:s', time() + 5.5 * HOUR_IN_SECONDS ) ); }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that labels when a post was published the way WordPress admin screens do: for a post published less than a week ago, the human-readable age followed by ' ago' (for example '3 hours ago'); for anything a week old or older, the publication date in the site's timezone formatted with the site's date format setting.
tests.expected_behavior: The age comes from `human_time_diff()` on the post's publication timestamp, the threshold is a week (`WEEK_IN_SECONDS`), and the fallback must render in the site timezone with the site's `date_format` option (`wp_date()`), not the server's timezone. Runtime validation seeds posts three hours, six days and thirty days old in Europe/Berlin and checks the exact strings, with the old post's expected value computed with DateTimeImmutable.
requirements: Use the relative form only while the post is less than a week old, appending ' ago' to the human-readable difference
Otherwise format the publication date in the site's timezone using the site's date format setting
Base both branches on the post's publication moment

required_patterns.description: Uses the site date format for the absolute branch
Formats the absolute date in the site timezone

runtime_checks.setup: $GLOBALS['wpbp_dt_004_tz'] = array( 'timezone_string' => get_option( 'timezone_string' ), 'gmt_offset' => get_option( 'gmt_offset' ) ); update_option( 'timezone_string', 'Europe/Berlin' ); update_option( 'gmt_offset', '' ); $now = time(); $ages = array( 'recent' => 3 * HOUR_IN_SECONDS, 'week_edge' => 6 * DAY_IN_SECONDS, 'old' => 30 * DAY_IN_SECONDS ); $fixtures = array(); foreach ( $ages as $key => $age ) { $timestamp = $now - $age; $post_id = wp_insert_post( array( 'post_title' => 'WPBP age ' . $key, 'post_status' => 'publish', 'post_date' => (string) wp_date( 'Y-m-d H:i:s', $timestamp ), 'post_date_gmt' => gmdate( 'Y-m-d H:i:s', $timestamp ) ) ); $fixtures[ $key ] = array( 'id' => (int) $post_id, 'timestamp' => $timestamp ); } $GLOBALS['wpbp_dt_004'] = $fixtures;

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_dates_time_004' ) ) { return false; } $fixtures = (array) ( $GLOBALS['wpbp_dt_004'] ?? array() ); if ( 3 !== count( $fixtures ) ) { return false; } if ( '3 hours ago' !== wpbp_dates_time_004( (int) $fixtures['recent']['id'] ) ) { return false; } if ( '6 days ago' !== wpbp_dates_time_004( (int) $fixtures['week_edge']['id'] ) ) { return false; } $expected = ( new DateTimeImmutable( '@' . (int) $fixtures['old']['timestamp'] ) )->setTimezone( new DateTimeZone( 'Europe/Berlin' ) )->format( (string) get_option( 'date_format' ) ); return $expected === wpbp_dates_time_004( (int) $fixtures['old']['id'] );

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_dates_time_004( int $post_id ): string { $timestamp = get_post_timestamp( $post_id ); if ( false === $timestamp ) { return ''; } if ( ( time() - $timestamp ) < WEEK_IN_SECONDS ) { return sprintf( '%s ago', human_time_diff( $timestamp, time() ) ); } return (string) wp_date( (string) get_option( 'date_format' ), $timestamp ); }
exploit_solutions: function wpbp_dates_time_004( int $post_id ): string { $timestamp = get_post_timestamp( $post_id ); return sprintf( '%s ago', human_time_diff( $timestamp, time() ) ); }

function wpbp_dates_time_004( int $post_id ): string { $timestamp = get_post_timestamp( $post_id ); if ( ( time() - $timestamp ) < DAY_IN_SECONDS ) { return sprintf( '%s ago', human_time_diff( $timestamp, time() ) ); } return (string) wp_date( (string) get_option( 'date_format' ), $timestamp ); }

function wpbp_dates_time_004( int $post_id ): string { $timestamp = get_post_timestamp( $post_id ); if ( ( time() - $timestamp ) < WEEK_IN_SECONDS ) { return sprintf( '%s ago', human_time_diff( $timestamp, time() ) ); } return gmdate( 'Y-m-d', $timestamp ); }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that takes a moment stored in UTC as a 'Y-m-d H:i:s' string and returns it as an ISO 8601 string (PHP's 'c' format) in the site's timezone. It must work both when the site is configured with a named timezone and when the site only has a manual UTC offset, including offsets that are not whole hours.
tests.expected_behavior: `wp_timezone()` handles both configurations: it returns the named zone when `timezone_string` is set and builds a ±HH:MM zone from `gmt_offset` otherwise, so `new DateTimeZone( get_option( 'timezone_string' ) )` throws on an offset-only site and whole-hour arithmetic misplaces half-hour and three-quarter-hour offsets. Runtime validation runs the same moment through Europe/Berlin, a -3.5 offset site and a +5.75 offset site, comparing against DateTimeImmutable output.
requirements: Interpret the incoming string as UTC
Render it in the site's timezone as an ISO 8601 string with the correct UTC offset
Support sites configured with only a manual UTC offset, including fractional offsets

required_patterns.description: Resolves the site timezone for both configurations

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_dates_time_005' ) ) { return false; } $utc = new DateTimeZone( 'UTC' ); $moment = '2025-07-15 12:00:00'; $cases = array( array( 'Europe/Berlin', '', 'Europe/Berlin' ), array( '', '-3.5', '-03:30' ), array( '', '5.75', '+05:45' ) ); foreach ( $cases as $case ) { update_option( 'timezone_string', $case[0] ); update_option( 'gmt_offset', $case[1] ); $expected = ( new DateTimeImmutable( $moment, $utc ) )->setTimezone( new DateTimeZone( $case[2] ) )->format( 'c' ); $actual = wpbp_dates_time_005( $moment ); if ( ! is_string( $actual ) || $expected !== $actual ) { return false; } } return true;
assertions.description: The moment renders correctly for a named timezone and for fractional manual offsets

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_dates_time_005( string $utc_datetime ): string { $datetime = new DateTimeImmutable( $utc_datetime, new DateTimeZone( 'UTC' ) ); return $datetime->setTimezone( wp_timezone() )->format( 'c' ); }
exploit_solutions: function wpbp_dates_time_005( string $utc_datetime ): string { $datetime = new DateTimeImmutable( $utc_datetime, new DateTimeZone( 'UTC' ) ); return $datetime->setTimezone( new DateTimeZone( (string) get_option( 'timezone_string' ) ) )->format( 'c' ); }

function wpbp_dates_time_005( string $utc_datetime ): string { $offset = (int) get_option( 'gmt_offset' ); $datetime = new DateTimeImmutable( $utc_datetime, new DateTimeZone( 'UTC' ) ); return $datetime->setTimezone( new DateTimeZone( sprintf( '%+03d:00', $offset ) ) )->format( 'c' ); }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that returns the IDs of the published posts whose publication date falls on a given calendar day on the site's clock. The day arrives as a 'Y-m-d' string, and a post published at exactly midnight local time belongs to that day.
tests.expected_behavior: Posts are matched on `post_date`, which holds site-local time, with a date query on the calendar day (or an inclusive between-bounds query) — matching on `post_date_gmt` shifts the window by the site's offset, and an exclusive `after` bound drops the post published at exactly 00:00:00. Runtime validation seeds posts either side of local midnight in America/Los_Angeles, whose UTC dates deliberately disagree with their local dates, and queries three different days plus an empty one.
requirements: Match the calendar day on the site's clock, not in UTC
Include a post published at exactly 00:00:00 local time and exclude the previous day's late evening post
Return the matching published post IDs

runtime_checks.setup: $GLOBALS['wpbp_dt_006_tz'] = array( 'timezone_string' => get_option( 'timezone_string' ), 'gmt_offset' => get_option( 'gmt_offset' ) ); update_option( 'timezone_string', 'America/Los_Angeles' ); update_option( 'gmt_offset', '' ); $seed = array( 'eve' => array( '2025-07-15 23:30:00', '2025-07-16 06:30:00' ), 'midnight' => array( '2025-07-16 00:00:00', '2025-07-16 07:00:00' ), 'morning' => array( '2025-07-16 00:30:00', '2025-07-16 07:30:00' ), 'night' => array( '2025-07-16 23:45:00', '2025-07-17 06:45:00' ), 'earlier' => array( '2025-07-14 12:00:00', '2025-07-14 19:00:00' ) ); $fixtures = array(); foreach ( $seed as $key => $dates ) { $fixtures[ $key ] = (int) wp_insert_post( array( 'post_title' => 'WPBP day ' . $key, 'post_status' => 'publish', 'post_date' => $dates[0], 'post_date_gmt' => $dates[1] ) ); } $GLOBALS['wpbp_dt_006'] = $fixtures;

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_dates_time_006' ) ) { return false; } $fixtures = (array) ( $GLOBALS['wpbp_dt_006'] ?? array() ); if ( 5 !== count( $fixtures ) ) { return false; } $normalize = static function ( $value ) { if ( ! is_array( $value ) ) { return null; } $ids = array_map( 'intval', $value ); sort( $ids ); return $ids; }; $expect = static function ( array $keys ) use ( $fixtures ) { $ids = array(); foreach ( $keys as $key ) { $ids[] = (int) $fixtures[ $key ]; } sort( $ids ); return $ids; }; if ( $normalize( wpbp_dates_time_006( '2025-07-16' ) ) !== $expect( array( 'midnight', 'morning', 'night' ) ) ) { return false; } if ( $normalize( wpbp_dates_time_006( '2025-07-15' ) ) !== $expect( array( 'eve' ) ) ) { return false; } if ( $normalize( wpbp_dates_time_006( '2025-07-14' ) ) !== $expect( array( 'earlier' ) ) ) { return false; } return array() === $normalize( wpbp_dates_time_006( '2025-07-17' ) );
assertions.description: Days are cut on the site's clock, including the post published at exactly local midnight

'' ); update_option( 'gmt_offset', $saved['gmt_offset'] ?? 0 ); unset( $GLOBALS['wpbp_dt_006_tz'] );
